title: Every One From The One Before
logline: In a foothill hamlet under a wet-zone escarpment, a household cuts a few culms of forest reed at first light and works through them in one sitting, splitting each splint out of the splint before it until the strips are as fine as the reed will give, and weaving from that one run of splints a nested set of sieves of identical width whose only difference is how fine the mesh is.
human_question: If going deeper means having less rather than more, how do you know you have taken as much away as the material allows?

place.what_kind_of_place: Wet-zone foothill country under a high escarpment, in a district of steep gullies, small streams and forest edge. The reed the work depends on grows in dense clumps in the gullies and along stream banks under the canopy: a thin-walled forest reed, several metres tall, growing in thickets so close that a cut stand reads as a wall of pale stems. It is not planted, is not anybody's crop, and is cut a few culms at a time. The working place is a house yard and the shaded floor of a veranda or a lean-to: a mat, a low stool, a heavy knife, a smaller knife, a bill hook, a bundle of green culms leaning against a wall, and the floor gradually covering over with splints in graded thicknesses as the morning goes on. Nothing is powered. The instruments are a thumbnail run along a splint, the sound it makes when it goes, the way it bends without breaking, and the width of the finished mesh held up against the light. What comes off the floor at the end of a session is domestic and unglamorous: coarse riddles for gravel and grain, winnowing trays, tighter sieves for rice, and the finest one, for flour, which is the one the whole session is judged by.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the craft is subtraction from beginning to end, and because the order of it cannot be rearranged. Nothing is ever added: every splint in the room came out of a thicker splint that was already there, and the finest one is the thinnest thing that could be got out of a stem that arrived whole. Wide and high, the country is quietly graphic — a green escarpment, gullies of pale reed under a darker canopy, one or two roofs, mist lifting off the streams — and the reed stands separate from everything else around it because its colour is wrong for the forest. Close, the film is a sequence of very small precise actions in a fixed order: a knife entered at the end of a culm and walked down it, a splint halved, the halves halved, the inner pith scraped away, a strip drawn across a blade to take its back off, and then the weaving, which slows down each time the strip gets finer. And there is a real limit in it, found by failing: at some width the splint stops bending and snaps, and the maker knows where that is only because they have gone past it before. The single most beautiful thing the place produces is also the plainest statement of the idea — the finished set stacked one inside another on the floor, every piece the same width as every other, differing in nothing but fineness.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The material, in one direction only, and the speed of the work. A culm cut this morning has to be worked while it is still green enough to split cleanly and dry enough not to tear, which is a window of hours rather than days, so a session has its own clock. Each generation of splint exists only because the one before it was made, and the first coarse split has to be done well and fast or nothing after it is possible; a splint that runs off-line is gone and the material with it. As the strips get finer the work gets slower and quieter and the failures get more expensive, because a snapped fine splint has taken all the earlier splitting with it. Across a longer clock the trade itself is thinning: the reed comes from forest land whose access is regulated, plastic and wire mesh have taken most of the market for the coarse end of the range, and the fine end survives because nothing manufactured does that job as well at that price. Households that still do it tend to be few and related to one another.
place.when_it_looks_best: A dry, still stretch, because the splitting is done in the open or under an open roof and the reed is cut and carried on foot from wet gullies. Within the day the film is almost forced: the escarpment and the reed gullies from height in the half hour after first light and again in the last half hour, when the pale stands separate from the canopy; the cutting and the carry in the cool of early morning; and the whole splitting-and-weaving run through the middle of the day in shade, which is when it is normally done and which is also the light the graded set needs, because mesh reads against a bright doorway and dies in direct sun. The gullies are worth filming at noon for the opposite reason: the reed flattens into the forest and disappears.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about one morning's work with a knife. A green escarpment at first light and pale reed thickets in the gullies below it; a few culms cut and carried up a path; a knife entered at the end of a stem and walked down its length; a splint halved, and the halves halved, and the halves of those halved again; pith scraped out and thrown aside; a strip drawn across a blade until it is thin enough to bend round a thumb; the floor slowly filling with strips in four or five thicknesses; then the weaving, faster at the coarse end and very slow at the fine end; a splint that snaps and is dropped; and at the end a set of sieves stacked one inside another, all the same width, ranked only by mesh. It has a complete shape that nobody says out loud: a thing taken apart by halves until it will not go further, and made into a graded run in a single sitting. Anyone who likes hand skill, a fixed order of operations, or the fact that a craft can find a physical limit by walking up to it and breaking it has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same morning becomes the sources' account of how the deep meditative attainments are said to get subtler, filmed in a process whose order the material fixes rather than the maker. The texts describe a movement repeated at every step: the state already gained is handled at will, then seen as coarse compared with a calmer one, and then the wish for it is dropped, and the same object is taken up again. They give that movement their own picture — four cloths of identical length and breadth woven from thread of four grades, differing in nothing but fineness — and another picture of the dependence between the stages, of men hanging from a pavilion roof above filthy ground, each holding the one before. A run of splints in which nothing is added and everything is halved out of something coarser, ending in a graded set of identical width, carries both pictures without anybody reciting either. The voice never says the maker is meditating, never says the splints are states of mind, and never suggests anybody on screen has attained anything. It says these are the sources' own images, that the sources put a hard limit on what refinement buys, and that no shot of anything can show an inner attainment.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high, looking along the foot of a wet-zone escarpment. Steep green slopes, gullies running down them, and in the gullies pale close-packed reed standing a shade lighter than everything around it. One tin roof and a yard, small, on a shoulder of the slope.
sequence.voice: Everything that will be made down there today comes out of that reed and out of nothing else. Nothing gets added between the stem and the finished thing. The whole morning is one operation done over and over, and each time it is done the material has less in it than it had before.

sequence.on_screen: The cut: a bill hook into the base of a culm, the stem lowered, a few of them carried up a wet path on a shoulder. Then the yard: the bundle leaning on a wall, a mat, a stool, two knives. A heavy knife entered at the end of a culm and walked steadily down its whole length until it falls in two.
sequence.voice: The books put a condition on going deeper, and it is about ease and not about effort. Before anybody moves on from the state they already have, they must be able to turn to it, enter it, stay in it exactly as long as they intended, leave it on time, and look back over what it was made of, all at will, and in any of its parts [C088-P4:L26–L38; C088-M:L5]. This first split has been made a few thousand times in this yard. It is the only reason the rest of the morning is possible.

sequence.on_screen: Close and repeated: a half becoming two quarters, a quarter becoming two eighths, the knife smaller each time and the hands slower. Pith scraped out with a thumbnail and dropped. On the mat, splints accumulating in bands of decreasing thickness, laid out where they fell.
sequence.voice: The movement the texts describe is one sentence repeated. Standing in the calm he has, he looks at what it is made of, and a factor of it appears coarse to him, and being coarse it is weak, and being weak it is faulty, and the quieter state without it is peaceful; and so he puts down his liking for the state he is in and begins again on the same object [C088-P4:L44]. The word the text uses is the word a craftsman uses. Coarse. Not wrong, not bad. Coarse, seen from a little further on.

sequence.on_screen: The weaving. The coarse riddle going quickly under the hands, the next one slower, the next slower again. Then the finished pieces brought together and stacked one inside another in a doorway, held up so the light comes through them: four or five circles of identical width, and the mesh closing from one to the next.
sequence.voice: Here the sources hand the film its own picture. One woman spins thread of four grades, coarse, fine, finer, finest, and four cloths are woven from them, and the four cloths are of exactly the same length and the same breadth, so that by measure there is no difference between them at all; and yet in softness, in fineness and in worth each later one is finer than the one before [C088-P4:L280–L284]. That is their image and not ours, and this is what it is an image of: four states that hold the same two factors, and differ only in how fine those factors have become.

sequence.on_screen: The stacked set held still, from directly above, then the discarded material around it: the pith, the outer skin, the offcuts, the coarse first halves that went into everything. A hand lifting the finest piece off the top of the stack and setting it down alone.
sequence.voice: The other image in these books is about what each stage is standing on. There is a pavilion in a wasteland, over foul ground, and a man who will not put his feet down holds on to the roof; a second man holds on to him; a third finds his own place at the far end of the same roof; a fourth holds the third [C014-P:L68]. Each one is off the ground only because of the one before. And the books are careful to say where this is happening. The wasteland is the round of existence itself, and the filthy ground beneath is the world of the senses [C014-P:L72]. None of the four has left the desert.

sequence.on_screen: Two people on the same veranda working the same material at different speeds: one taking a splint down in three passes, the other in five, with more stages laid out on the mat in front of them. No comparison made in the cutting, no reaction shots.
sequence.voice: The books notice this and refuse to make a hierarchy out of it. Some people need fewer preparatory moments and some need more, and the whole scheme of these attainments was set out in four steps for the quicker and in five steps for the slower, on the same ground and to the same end [C015-P:L45–L47]. It is the size of the step that changes. It is not a ranking of anybody, and nothing in it is a measure of intelligence.

sequence.on_screen: A splint taken one halving too far: it whitens, kinks and snaps, and both pieces are dropped. Then the finest sieve on the floor, and past it an attempt at a finer one abandoned half-woven. Last light on the escarpment and the reed gullies going dark.
sequence.voice: Two things the books say against themselves. The finest of these states is so faint that it cannot be taken apart and gone through piece by piece at all, and the text says plainly that even the wisest of the disciples could not do it [C088-P4:L262–L266]. So finer is not automatically clearer, and calm on its own does not finish the work. And the second thing is ours. Nothing on this floor is an attainment. A set of sieves is a set of sieves, nobody here is meditating, and no shot of anybody's hands could ever show you an inner state.

concept_merge.why_together: C088 supplies the movement and the film's central image. It requires that the attainment already reached be mastered in five ways, at will, before anything further is attempted [C088-P4:L26–L38; C088-M:L5]; it states the step itself as seeing a factor of the present state as coarse, therefore weak, therefore faulty, and the quieter state as peaceful, and then dropping the liking for what one has [C088-P4:L44; C088-P4:L58]; and for the four formless attainments it gives its own simile of four cloths of identical length and breadth woven from four grades of thread, differing in nothing but fineness [C088-P4:L280–L284], alongside a four-storey pavilion whose floors are identical as floors [C088-P4:L278]. It also supplies the honesty: the finest of these states is too faint to be taken apart and examined, and the text says even the wisest disciple could not do it [C088-P4:L262–L266]. C014 supplies the dependence between the stages and the limit on what they amount to: its closing simile has four men off the ground only because each is holding the one before [C014-P:L68], and it says in as many words that the wasteland they are hanging in is the round of existence and the foul ground beneath is the sense world [C014-P:L72], so the series is not a way out of anything. C015 supplies the one human difference the film will show: that some people need fewer preparatory moments than others, and that the same ground was set out in four steps for the quicker and five for the slower [C015-P:L45–L47]. A craft in which every splint is halved out of a coarser splint, in which nothing is added at any point, in which the run is made in a single sitting, and which ends in a graded set of identical width, puts the cloth simile, the holding-on simile and the difference of pace into one morning without any of them having to be explained.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That refinement in these texts is subtraction resting on mastery, not accumulation, and that it buys less than it looks as though it should. Said flat, the sequence is a list of names in an ascending order, which reads immediately as a ladder of achievement. Put on a run of splints it becomes a physical constraint: the fine strip cannot exist unless the coarse one was made first and made well, the first split has to be automatic before the fourth is even attempted, nothing can be put back into a splint once it has been taken off, and the floor of the sequence is found by breaking something. Holding the three concepts together also stops three separate misreadings. The cloth simile alone would be decorative. The holding-on simile alone would be a diagram, and without C014's own line about the wasteland it would look like an escape ladder. The difference of pace alone would rank two people sitting on the same veranda. This idea has been round once before. Its first version was the same concept in a pottery village, a graded set of bowls thrown in one sitting with each wall thinner than the last; the concept was right and the setting was not, because pottery villages are carried several times over in this slate. The craft here keeps everything the pottery version had — a graded run made in one session, refinement by removal, and a limit found by failing — and adds two things the wheel did not give: every stage is literally cut out of the stage before it, which is the holding-on simile rather than a metaphor for it, and the finished pieces are identical in size and differ in nothing but fineness, which is the cloth simile exactly as the source states it.

concept_links.why: The film is this concept's movement and this concept's own similes, and nothing else from it. The five masteries are narrated over the first coarse split, which is the one operation in the room that has to be automatic before any of the others can happen, and they are given as the source gives them, as five kinds of ease rather than five kinds of effort [C088-P4:L26–L38; C088-M:L5]. The step itself is narrated in the source's own terms over the repeated halving — coarse, therefore weak, therefore faulty, the quieter state peaceful, and the liking for what one has put down [C088-P4:L44] — and the film uses the source's word for it, coarse, rather than any word of its own. The four-cloth simile is spoken once, at the moment the footage can carry it, over a stacked set of identical width whose only difference is mesh, and it is named out loud as the source's image and not the film's [C088-P4:L280–L284]. The closing beat carries the concept's own limit, that the finest of these states cannot be examined factor by factor and that even the wisest disciple could not do it [C088-P4:L262–L266], which is the source's own refusal of the idea that deeper is automatically clearer. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured. There is no suggestion that the maker is meditating or that anything filmed is an absorption, and the film says so in its last line, because the digest is explicit that nothing filmable can show these states. 'Let go of pleasure' is not made into an ascetic slogan: what the narration says is dropped is the liking for the stage already held, not the capacity for satisfaction, and the source's own note that the third absorption is bodily sweet is not contradicted anywhere. Equanimity is not filmed or narrated as not caring, and the ten kinds of equanimity are not quoted. There is no flow-state or focus framing: the film never offers the craft as a technique for anything. Nothingness is not touched, so the nihilist misreading has nothing to attach to. Refinement is never presented as making a person higher, which is why the beat about two people working at different speeds is given to C015 and is filmed without comparison. The Moggallāna episode named in the extract is not retold. The scope question the digest raises, whether the formless attainments belong to this concept or elsewhere, is left open: the film takes the cloth simile as the source states it, as an image for the four formless attainments, and claims nothing about where the material is filed.

This concept gives the film the relation between one stage and the next, and it gives it the ceiling. Its closing simile of four men hanging from a pavilion above foul ground, each off the ground only because of the one before, is narrated over the stacked set and the heap of offcuts, which is the point in the morning when it is visible that every fine splint in the room was cut out of a coarse one [C014-P:L68]. In the same beat the film narrates the source's own gloss on that simile, that the wasteland is the round of existence and the filthy ground beneath it the world of the senses [C014-P:L72], which is the concept's flat statement that the whole series is still inside the round and is not liberation. Every limit in the digest is honoured and one of them is on screen. 'Transcend the body' is refused by construction, since the film never states the motive the source gives for these attainments and never puts disgust with the body anywhere near a person; the digest warns that on screen that motive risks sounding like contempt for the sick, the old or the disabled, so it is left out of the film entirely rather than softened. 'Everything is empty space' and 'nothing exists' have nothing to attach to, because the film does not narrate the objects of the four states at all and never presents space or absence as a claim about the world; the digest's point that these are mental concepts used as objects is respected by silence rather than by explanation. Nothing suggests these are states available to anyone, and the source's requirement of prior mastery is what the film's second beat is about. The garbled passage at C014-P:L60 and the uncertainty about the third state's position in the simile are not quoted or relied on; the film uses only the simile's plain shape, each one held by the one before.

This concept contributes one narrated line and one whole beat. The source says that people who gain these states divide into the quicker and the slower, that the quicker need fewer preparatory moments, and that the same ground was taught as four steps for the quicker and five for the slower [C015-P:L45–L47]. That is spoken over two people working the same reed at different speeds on the same veranda, with more intermediate stages laid out in front of the slower one, which is the one place in the film where a difference between two human beings is on screen. The digest's sharpest limit for this concept is that fast and slow must not become a ranking of people's worth, and the film honours it three ways: the narration says out loud that it is the size of the step that changes and not the destination, it says the difference is not a measure of intelligence, and the footage is cut without any comparison — no reaction shot, no cutaway from one pair of hands to the other inside a single action, and no teacher judging anybody. Nothing else from this concept is used. The formless resultant minds, the lifespans in great aeons and the whole rebirth frame are left out, because the digest says a long peaceful afterlife is not the goal here and the material cannot be filmed at all. The cake-and-rice illustration is not quoted, as the digest asks. Functional minds are not touched, so the 'actions without consequences' slogan has no opening. And Margaya's remark that formless beings have a happiness close to nibbāna's, which the digest flags as needing a teacher's framing, is not used.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in these texts you go deeper by having less rather than more; that each stage is finished and handled at will before it can look coarse beside the next one, so that nothing is skipped and nothing is reached by jumping; that the later stages are identical to the earlier ones in everything except fineness, which is the sources' own image of four cloths of the same size; that the whole series is still inside the round and is not a way out of it; and that the sources themselves say the finest of these states is too faint to be examined, so deeper calm is not the same thing as clearer seeing. The graded run of splints is an analogy and the film says so. Nobody on screen is presented as having attained anything, and no claim is made about anybody's inner life.
what_must_be_real: The session's own order at its own speed. The reed is not cut early for the camera, no splints are prepared in advance or laid out for a shot, the graded run is not rearranged, nothing is re-split for a second take, and no piece is woven twice. If the fine splints go badly, or the finest sieve is abandoned, the film has that session and keeps it. Nobody is asked to work faster, slower or in better light than they would, nobody is asked to sit where they would not sit, and nothing about how the knives are handled is changed for the camera. No household's earnings, debts or buyers are put on screen and there is no sale in the film. Where the reed is cut, and whether it is legal to cut it there, is the household's business and is not filmed in any way that could expose them. Nobody in the film is named or followed as a character, nobody is asked to confirm any doctrine, and no participant's skill, patience or steadiness is presented as a spiritual quality.
position_hint: middle of the group, after the film about long attention and before the group turns to insight and to what cannot be undone. It is the group's statement that depth is subtraction and that the stages are nested rather than stacked, and it is also the group's first explicit refusal of the ladder reading, which the later and harder films need to have been made before they arrive. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting the graded set read as a ladder of achievement, which is the single most likely misreading of an ascending sequence and the one the sources contradict most directly.
Implying, by framing, patience or admiration, that the maker is in any inner state at all. Nothing filmable shows these attainments and the film has to say so rather than rely on restraint.
Forcing the session into exactly four grades so that it matches the four cloths, or numbering the stages on screen.
Letting the difference in pace between two people on one veranda read as a ranking of them, or letting the slower one be filmed as the lesser one.

Turning the dropping of each stage into an ascetic message about giving things up, when the source's own third absorption is described as bodily sweet and what is dropped is only the liking for what has already been gained.
Letting the nested sieves read as an escape or a way out, when the concept that supplies the nesting says in as many words that all four are still hanging inside the wasteland.
Romanticising a thinning livelihood, or filming the craft as heritage rather than as work somebody did this morning for a reason.
Exposing where the reed was cut and under whose permission, which could put a household in front of a forest authority for the sake of a shot.
Making the snapped splint into a symbol of failure or of death. It is a splint, and the group's floor is that nothing here stands in for a person's ending.
Handing the film's own vocabulary to the source, or the source's to the film: 'coarse' is the text's word and the narration has to keep it as a quotation rather than a judgement on the work.
drop_if: No household works a range of mesh grades in one sitting, so the graded run would have to be set up for the camera and the film's whole structure would be staged.
The reed now arrives pre-split from a supplier, so the halving sequence that the film is about no longer happens in one place.
Cutting or carrying the reed cannot be filmed without exposing a household to a forest-access problem.
The only makers reachable have stopped making the fine end of the range, which is the end the concept needs.
Filming the splitting cannot be done without changing how it is done, or without asking somebody to make pieces they have no buyer for.

connections.note: Two close studies of attention getting finer: one held on a single object for a long time, one walked down a graded run in a single sitting.
Refinement of depth here, sameness of destination with difference of texture there; the two films state the same refusal of ranking from opposite ends.
This one is about a sequence that can always be taken one step further; the next is about the difference between a change that holds down and a change that removes the ground.

selection.reason: Its central action is the concept: a graded run made in one sitting in which every stage is cut out of the stage before it and nothing is ever added, ending in a set identical in size and different only in fineness, which is the source's own simile made physical.

review.note: Relocated 2026-09-24 off pottery entirely. The previous version was a graded set of bowls thrown in one sitting with each wall thinner than the last; the concept was sound and is unchanged, but pottery villages are carried several times over in this slate and cannot take another film. The craft has moved to the splitting of forest reed and the weaving of a graded run of sieves, in a different province, and the move strengthens two things rather than costing anything. Every splint is now literally cut out of the splint before it, which is C014's holding-on simile as a physical fact rather than as a comparison; and the finished pieces are identical in width and differ only in mesh, which is C088's four-cloth simile exactly as the source states it, where a set of bowls of graded wall thickness was only an approximation of it. The limit found by failing survives the move, because a splint taken one halving too far snaps. All three concepts were re-read from their digests as a new reader and every citation was re-tested line by line against the source files; none was carried over from the previous text unchecked. Two citations are new to this pass: the five masteries [C088-P4:L26–L38; C088-M:L5], which the previous version referred to only in the digest's paraphrase, and C088-P4:L262–L266, the source's own statement that the finest of these states cannot be examined factor by factor and that even the wisest disciple could not do it, which now closes the film. C014-P:L72 has been added because C014's digest insists the whole series is still inside the round, and without that line the nested set would read as an escape ladder. The pavilion simile at C088-P4:L278, which the extract gives immediately before the cloth simile, was read and is deliberately not narrated, to avoid running two of the source's images together in one beat. The concept scope question C088's digest raises, whether the four formless attainments belong to that concept or elsewhere, is recorded in the unknowns and is not decided here; the film quotes the cloth simile as the source gives it and makes no filing claim. The closing beat states the film's own limit out loud, that nothing filmable shows an inner attainment, because that is the strictest line in all three digests.

suggested_location.name: The forest-reed splitting and sieve-weaving households of the Kuruwita foothills, below the western escarpment in the Ratnapura District

also_known_as.name: bata
also_known_as.meaning: the thin-walled forest reed the whole craft depends on, recorded botanically as Ochlandra stridula, the Ceylon reed-bamboo, which grows in dense clumps along streams and forest edges in this district and the one north of it
also_known_as.used_by: Sinhala usage and the craft literature

also_known_as.name: kulla
also_known_as.meaning: the flat winnowing tray woven from split reed, one of the standard pieces in the range

also_known_as.name: peneraya
also_known_as.meaning: a sieve; in reed work a range rather than one object, from a coarse riddle down to a close-woven flour sieve, which is the graded run the film is built on. Whether a whole graded run is normally made in one sitting has not been checked with anybody in the trade
also_known_as.used_by: Sinhala domestic usage; the graded-run sense is reported here and unverified

suggested_location.region: Ratnapura District, Sabaragamuwa Province: the wet-zone foothill country on the lower slopes below the western escarpment, in the gullied stream land inland of the district's northern approach road and well away from the district's gem workings
suggested_location.why_here: Because the material and the craft are both documented here, and because the whole chain is short, domestic and visible in one yard. The craft literature on the island's reed and cane work names this district specifically for reed work and names a settlement in these foothills as one of the places it is found, with cane work in two nearby villages; the reed itself is recorded as growing extensively in this district and the one immediately north of it. Everything the film needs is within a few hundred metres: the standing reed in the gullies, the cut, the carry, the mat, the knives, the graded splints and the finished set. There is no middle stage in another town, no market floor in the film and no auction. The constraint is a property of the material rather than of a buyer, and it runs one way only: a culm has to be worked while it is still green enough to split and dry enough not to tear, every splint has to be cut out of a coarser splint, and nothing that comes off a strip can be put back on it. The district is also thin on this slate outside its gem workings, which this film has nothing to do with, and the foothill country is quietly graphic from height — a green escarpment with pale reed running down the gullies under a darker canopy, which separates at either end of the day and vanishes at noon. The makers are households rather than a factory, which is what the concept needs, since the film is about one person's run of splints and not about production.
what_to_film: The escarpment and the reed gullies from height in the half hour after first light and again in the last half hour, so the pale stands separate from the canopy, and again at noon when they flatten into it.
The cut and the carry: a bill hook into the base of a culm, the stem lowered through the undergrowth, and a few culms carried up a wet path on a shoulder.
The first coarse split at arm's length from a fixed position, held long: the heavy knife entered at the end of the culm and walked down its whole length.
The halving sequence in one continuous take if it can be got: half to quarter to eighth and beyond, with the knife getting smaller and the hands slower each time.
The pith and the outer skin being scraped away and dropped, because it is the clearest statement in the film that nothing is added and everything is removed.
The mat as it fills, from directly above, so the bands of decreasing thickness read as a graded run rather than as a mess.
The weaving at both ends of the range in the same light, so the change of speed between the coarse riddle and the fine sieve is visible without being pointed at.
The finished set stacked one inside another and held against a bright doorway, from directly above and then at eye level, which is the single shot the whole film is built towards.
A splint taken one halving too far, whitening, kinking and snapping, filmed plainly and without emphasis.
Two people working the same material at different speeds on the same veranda, in a single wide frame rather than in cut-together close-ups.
A finished piece in domestic use, and a worn-out one, in the same light as a new one, without commentary.
suggested_location.access: By road inland from the district's northern approach and then on lanes and footpaths; the reed stands are in gullies and forest edge and the working places are private house yards and lean-tos, so everything depends on the household whose yard and knives these are agreeing, and on being introduced through a craft body, a divisional officer or a group they already deal with rather than approaching cold. The reed grows on land whose access is regulated, and where and under what permission a household cuts is their affair: it must not be filmed in any way that could put them in front of a forest authority, and the crew should assume that the cutting may have to be filmed only with the household's explicit agreement or not at all. The hazards are domestic and sharp rather than dangerous at a distance — heavy knives worked towards the body on a floor where people are sitting — and the crew has to be able to stay clear of a splitting arc for hours without asking anybody to move. Drone flight over occupied house plots and over forest edge needs the household's agreement whatever the general position is, and the escarpment weather closes in fast, so the elevated views may have to be taken on the first clear morning available rather than to a plan.
suggested_location.best_time: A dry, still stretch in either of the year's drier windows, since the reed is cut and carried out of wet gullies and the splitting is done in the open or under an open roof. A session followed straight through rather than a week of pieces: the height and the cut in the cool of early morning, the splitting and the weaving through the middle of the day in shade, and the set against a bright doorway in the late afternoon. A second session is worth planning for, because a run in which the fine splints go badly is part of the subject and cannot be arranged.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the craft sources above: reed and bamboo work in this district is recorded at a settlement in these foothills, with cane work at two named villages nearby; the reed used is named as bata, Ochlandra stridula, bought from local suppliers; the reed is described as slit into long strips and then cleaned thoroughly before weaving; the tools named are sharp knives; the recorded products include large paddy storage containers, plucking baskets and winnowing implements; and the craft is described as practised mainly by women within particular social groups, for local markets rather than export. From the botanical source: Ochlandra stridula is the Ceylon reed-bamboo, found extensively in this district and the one immediately north of it, and used for wattle walls, fences, mats, blinds, screens and partitions. The single largest assumption in this record is the one the film is built on and is the first thing to check on the ground: that a maker takes one culm down through several generations of splint in a single sitting and produces a graded run of mesh sizes from it, coarse riddle to fine flour sieve, in that order and in that session. The craft sources describe splitting and cleaning but say nothing about grading, nothing about how many passes a splint takes, and nothing about the width at which a splint snaps. Three further things the film depends on are inferences rather than confirmed facts about this district: that culms are still cut locally rather than bought pre-split, that the fine end of the range is still made at all, and that two makers of different speeds work in one place. The coordinates are the published position of the settlement the craft literature names and are a direction towards the country the film needs, not a survey: no household, yard, reed stand, group or person has been identified or approached, and no permission has been sought from anybody, including on forest access. No photograph of this district's reed work, of a splitting session, of any splint or of any finished piece was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is a herbarium sheet of the species.

unknowns: Whether a graded run of mesh sizes is actually made in one sitting, in order from coarse to fine, which is the film's entire structure.
How many generations of splint a culm is normally taken through, and at what width a splint stops bending and snaps.
Whether culms are still cut and carried locally in this district, or whether pre-split strip is now bought in, which would remove the halving sequence from the film.
Whether the fine end of the range is still made at all, given that wire and plastic mesh have taken most of the coarse end.
Whether a household will let one session be followed from the cut to the finished set without the order or the timing being adjusted, and on whose introduction.
Whether the cutting can be filmed at all without exposing a household to a forest-access problem, and whether the film has to be built without it.
Whether height can be obtained over these gullies and whether the reed stands read from the air as strongly as they appear to from the ground.
Whether the four formless attainments, which the cloth simile is given for, belong to this concept in the project's own filing or are handled elsewhere, which the digest flags as unresolved.
